page_title: Hand Keypoint Detection with Deep Learning and OpenCV

summary.title: Hand Keypoint Detection with Deep Learning and OpenCV
summary.one_liner: You learn how to load CMU's Caffe hand keypoint model in OpenCV's DNN module and use it to find 21 hand joints and fingertips, then draw them as a skeleton, with C++ and Python code.
keywords: how to detect hand joints opencv
takeaways: Hand keypoint detection finds finger joints and fingertips, which differs from hand detection that treats the whole hand as one object.
The CMU model outputs 22 probability maps: 21 hand points plus one background channel.
Load the Caffe prototxt and weights with OpenCV's readNetFromCaffe, convert the image to a blob, and run a forward pass.
Take the maximum of each probability map with minMaxLoc, scale it to the image size, and draw points above a threshold.
Connect the detected points with pose pairs to draw a hand skeleton; the code handles only one hand at a time.
summary.summary: The article explains hand keypoint detection, which locates finger joints and fingertips, and summarizes the CMU Perceptual Computing Lab approach. It uses a Convolutional Pose Machines style network trained with multi-view bootstrapping and 3D triangulation. The tutorial then walks through loading the Caffe model in OpenCV, running a forward pass on a blob, finding each keypoint's maximum in its probability map, and drawing points and a skeleton in both C++ and Python. It notes possible applications such as gesture recognition and sign language understanding, and that the code detects only one hand at a time.
